public_rationale: CoreWeave reported a $626 million net loss and approximately $18 billion raised through debt, convertibles and equity in April–June 2026 [e1]. Microsoft reported $35.8 billion in GAAP net income for the same quarter [e2]. Anthropic reported an $80.7 billion net loss for January–June 2026, including $72.4 billion in financing-related fair-value changes, alongside approximately $3.9 billion in positive operating cash flow [e3]. These company examples do not establish whether unprofitability, recurring funding dependence and vulnerability to payment failure characterized the typical AI data center customer in April–June 2026 [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: No representative customer population or weighting method is established.
Company-wide earnings do not isolate AI infrastructure economics or establish ability to meet commitments.
Net losses and fundraising alone do not establish dependence on continuing external funding.
Anthropic's figures cover six months, not the target quarter; its filing became available after the claim's publication.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data center customers are brittle, unprofitable and dependent on near-perpetual funding.

statement.excerpt: AI data center customers are brittle, unprofitable and dependent on near-perpetual funding.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is a general description of the customer base, not a claim about every customer or only selected startups.
Include actual tenants and compute purchasers, distinguishing their finances from those of downstream application developers.
Read brittle as vulnerable to payment failure if external funding stops, and near-perpetual funding as repeated financing needed to sustain operations and commitments.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter ordinarily reportable before the September 29 post.

The surrounding discussion relies on financial reporting and estimates, but supplies no single accounting basis for the customer population; do not silently equate GAAP losses, cash burn and financing dependence.
criteria.support_condition: Representative customer evidence shows that unprofitability and reliance on recurring external financing were general characteristics in the target quarter, with insufficient internal resources to sustain commitments.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative customer evidence shows that the typical customer was profitable and could sustain its commitments without recurring external financing.

evidence.excerpt: Net loss for Q2 was $626 million.
evidence.locator: Earnings-call transcript, discussion beginning Now turning to Q2 results
evidence.publisher: CoreWeave earnings call, reproduced by Semiboard
evidence.explanation: The reported loss illustrates unprofitability at one infrastructure intermediary and matches CoreWeave's primary quarterly results. It does not establish the finances or funding dependence of the typical customer.

evidence.excerpt:
Net income was $35.8 billion and increased 31% on a GAAP basis,
and was $35.3 billion and increased 22% on a non-GAAP basis
evidence.locator: Opening quarterly results, complete net-income bullet
evidence.explanation: Microsoft's positive consolidated earnings caution against extending startup losses to all major cloud counterparties. This company-level result does not establish customer-population profitability or prove that every infrastructure commitment is internally funded.

evidence.excerpt:
We have a history of net losses and may not generate sufficient revenue to achieve or sustain

profitability in the future.
evidence.locator: Risk Factors, page 64; qualifications in Cash Flows and interim financial statements
evidence.explanation: The filing reports first-half net losses, substantially affected by noncash financing revaluations, alongside positive operating cash flow of approximately $3.9 billion. Its six-month period and single-company scope do not match the quarter-wide population claim, and losses cannot be treated as equivalent cash burn.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Define and weight a representative cohort of actual tenants and compute purchasers. Obtain comparable April–June 2026 profitability, operating cash flow, liquidity, payment obligations and financing histories to assess whether typical customers could sustain commitments without recurring external funding.
